`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
**Why block bootstrap instead of simple random sampling for 10-year projections?** Daily returns have autocorrelation — a bad week tends to cluster (momentum/panic selling), and recoveries also cluster. Block bootstrap samples 6-month chunks of real history, preserving the "lumpy" behavior of actual markets — drawdowns that last months, not isolated bad days. This makes the P10 (bear case) band more realistic: it models sustained downturns, not just slightly-below-average scatter.

## NOL Carryforward Rules (C-Corp, TCJA §172)

**2025 NOL created:** ~$101-106K (depending on cost-seg fee treatment)

**Carryforward rules:**
1. **Indefinite carryforward** — no expiration (TCJA eliminated the old 20-year limit)
2. **No carryback** — C-Corps cannot carry NOLs back to prior years under TCJA
3. **80% limitation** — the NOL can offset **up to 80% of taxable income** in any future year. The remaining 20% is taxed at 21%.

## Practical Example for SKEstates

Assuming ~$90K annual taxable income in future years (full year rent minus expenses minus ongoing depreciation):

| Year | Taxable Income | NOL Used (80%) | Remaining Taxable | Tax (21%) | NOL Balance |
|------|---------------|----------------|-------------------|-----------|-------------|
| 2025 | ($101K) | — | $0 | $0 | $101K |
| 2026 | ~$90K | $72K | $18K | $3,780 | $29K |
| 2027 | ~$90K | $29K | $61K | $12,810 | **$0** |
| 2028+ | ~$90K | — | $90K | $18,900 | $0 |

**Total tax saved by the NOL:** ~$21K over the carryforward period.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
The 80% cap is the key detail most people miss. Even with a $101K NOL, you still pay *some* tax in 2026 and 2027 — the NOL doesn't zero out your bill completely in those years, it just reduces it substantially. The NOL shields about 1.5 years of income, saving roughly $21K in total federal tax at the 21% rate.
